conflicts.point: Whether decentralized open-weight distribution and post-market product liability provide an effective alternative to centralized pre-market administrative oversight.

positions.stance: Open-weight models empower local clinics to audit code rapidly, while strict product liability forces developers to internalize disparate impact costs more effectively than static agency reviews.
Community hospitals lack the technical staff and infrastructure to audit complex models, and unverified decentralized deployments multiply systemic failure points.

conflicts.point: Whether trade secret protections and anti-circumvention laws create insurmountable evidentiary barriers for plaintiffs in post-market civil litigation.

positions.stance: Public release of model parameter weights dissolves corporate trade secrecy and eliminates evidentiary hurdles for plaintiffs and independent researchers.
Enterprise licensing agreements, trade secret laws, and DMCA restrictions legally block local users from inspecting proprietary weights or proving causation in court.

verdicts.conflict: Whether decentralized open-weight distribution and post-market product liability provide an effective alternative to centralized pre-market administrative oversight.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position accounts for the institutional reality that community hospitals lack the specialized IT staff required to deconstruct complex models locally. Furthermore, software licensing agreements and trade secret laws create legal barriers that prevent downstream operators from inspecting internal code. Pre-market review avoids these structural limitations by evaluating safety before deployment.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence that community hospitals routinely execute independent code audits and successfully mitigate algorithmic bias without dedicated engineering teams would reverse this finding.

verdicts.conflict: Whether trade secret protections and anti-circumvention laws create insurmountable evidentiary barriers for plaintiffs in post-market civil litigation.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position aligns with existing intellectual property law and Digital Millennium Copyright Act restrictions that legally prohibit users from inspecting proprietary weight files. Accelerationist claims regarding the total dissolution of proprietary moats ignore commercial licensing practices and enterprise enforcement mechanisms.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Legislative reforms that explicitly mandate open-source weight releases and nullify non-disclosure agreements for deployed public sector algorithms would alter this assessment.
